description: Delete a mail folder together with every message and subfolder in it. This is permanent: the folder does NOT go to Deleted Items, so it cannot be restored from there. To keep the mail, move it out first (outlook_move_message). The confirmation totals the mail in the folder and every subfolder beneath it, and names any inbox rules that file into them (those rules stop working). Outlook's own folders are refused. The result is verified by re-reading the folder. A folder holding thousands of messages takes minutes to delete, so the call can come back with status "unknown" while Outlook keeps deleting: check its Total in outlook_list_folders falling, and never resend. Asks the user to confirm first: a confirmation prompt where the client supports one; otherwise the first call returns a preview and a confirmToken, and only a repeat call with that token proceeds (see MCP_CONFIRM_MODE).

confirmToken.description: ONLY for the two-step confirmation fallback (a client without MCP elicitation). The confirmToken from this same tool's phase-1 "confirmation-required" response, passed back ONLY after the user has seen that preview and explicitly approved it in chat — never on the first call, never invented, never reused. Call again with the same arguments. Ignored when the client supports elicitation.

name: outlook_delete_folder
